sutta: The next sutta 4.23. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vulture's Gaha in the bamboo grove as pure sanctuary. Now on that occasion the venerable Godhika was dwelling on the black slope on the east on the black rock on the Isigili slope. Then while the venerable Godhika was dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, he reached temporary liberation of mind, but he fell away from that temporary liberation of mind. The second time while the venerable Godhika was dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, he reached temporary liberation of mind, but he fell away from that temporary liberation of mind. And the third time and the fourth time and the fifth time and the sixth time while the venerable Godhika was dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, he reached temporary liberation of mind, but he fell away from the temporary liberation of mind. The seventh time while the venerable Godhika was dwelling religion ardent and resolute, he reached temporary liberation of mind. Then it occurred to the venerable Godhika, "Six times already I have fallen away from temporary liberation of mind. Let me use the knife." Then Mara, the evil one, having known with his own mind the reflection in the venerable Godhika's mind, approached the Blessed One and addressed him with these verses, "O great hero, great in wisdom, blazing forth with power and glory, I worship your feet, one with vision, who has overcome all enmity and fear. O great hero, who has vanquished death, your disciple is longing for death, intends to take his own life. Restrain him from this, O luminous one." "How, O Blessed One, can your disciple, one delighting in the teaching, a trainee seeking his mind's ideal, take his own life, O widely famed?" Now, on that occasion, the venerable Godhika had just used the knife. Then the Blessed One, having understood this is Mara, the evil one, addressed him in verse, "Such indeed is how the steadfast act. They are not attached to life. Having drawn out craving with its root, Godhika has attained final Nirvana." I'll stop here for a moment. So, here uh this venerable Godhika, he was practicing very diligently. And it's mentioned here that six times uh he tried to attain uh temporary liberation of mind. He attained it for a short while, but fell out of that state. Six times he fell out of that state. The seventh time, I think he attained that state. So, after that he decided to commit suicide. And uh Mara came to tell the Buddha to stop him. but the uh but the Buddha did not stop him. So after that Ambatthika committed suicide. This temporary liberation of mind according to the commentaries refers to the mundane jhanas states of concentration. He attained states of concentration but fell out of it. But for him to commit suicide and the Buddha did not restrain him. I feel that probably he had already attained Arahanthood. So this if he had already attained Arahanthood then it could be that the temporary liberation of mind is the cessation of perception and feeling. The cessation of perception and feeling also means the cessation of consciousness, a state of Parinirvana. When Arahan passes away he enters a state where all the consciousness ceases, the six consciousness. So because probably he was his body was sick, he was not well. He could attain it for a while but because he was not strong he fell out of the state. So there are a few instances of this in the Suttas and the Vinaya where sometimes a monk is very sick and he he decides to commit suicide. And the the Buddha knows that he is an Arahan, the Buddha does not restrain him from committing committing suicide because he has finished his work. And as the Buddha says here that they are not attached to life. Such indeed is how the state fast act, they are not attached to life. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks thus, "Come monks, let us go to the Black Rock on the Isigili slope, where the clansman Godhika has used the knife." "Yes, venerable sir," those monks replied. Then the blessed one, together with a number of monks, went to the Black Rock on the Isigili slope. The blessed one saw in the distance the venerable Godhika lying on the bed with his shoulder turned. On that occasion, a cloud of smoke, a swirl of darkness, was moving to the east, then to the west, to the north, to the south, upwards, downwards, into the intermediate quarters. The blessed one then addressed the monks thus, "Do you see, monks, that cloud of smoke, that swirl of darkness, moving to the east, then to the west, to the north, to the south, upwards, downwards, into the intermediate quarters?" "Yes, venerable sir," they replied. "That, monks, is Mara, the evil one, searching for the consciousness of the clansman Godhika, wondering, 'Where now has the consciousness of the clansman Godhika been established?' However, monks, with consciousness unestablished, the clansman Godhika has attained final Nirvana." Then Mara, the evil one, taking a lute of yellow vilva wood, approached the blessed one and addressed him in verse, "Above, below, and across, in the four quarters and in between, I have been searching, but do not find where Godhika has gone." And the Buddha said, "That steadfast man was resolute, a meditator always rejoicing in meditation, applying himself day and night, without attachment even to life, having conquered the army of death, not returning to renewed existence, having drawn out craving with its root, Godhika has attained final Nirvana." So much was he stricken with sorrow that his lute dropped from his armpit. Thereupon, that disappointed spirit disappeared right on the spot. So here, you see, And, after this arahant, this venerable Godhika passed away, and Mara was looking for his consciousness, where he was reborn. He was going all over the place, but the Buddha said Mara cannot find his consciousness because his his consciousness is unestablished. It's no more established in anywhere, in any body. That is the state of an Arahat after he passes away. The consciousness, the six consciousness stops. It's not It's unlike the Mahayana sutras which says that the Arahat have not finished their work. They still have to come back. No such thing in the earlier sutras. The Buddha and the Arahat disciples all when they pass away, their consciousness, six consciousness ceases. They enter Nibbana. So, this is interesting sutra where one among uh uh commit suicide, but the Buddha says there is no fault. You can commit suicide provided he has finished his work. Uh if he has finished his work, then uh the Buddha sometimes uh the the the Buddha says uh uh even before he commit suicide, the Buddha tells him whatever you want to do, don't worry. It's blameless. Uh but on the other hand, if a person has not attained enlightenment, has not finished his work, then the Buddha says that even if you are very sick, uh uh even you have a lot of pain, uh bear it. Bear it because human life is very hard to get. So, human life is the only realm of rebirth where we can practice hard to get out of samsara. Uh So, even if we are very sick, we should hold on to life because if we have life, then we still have time to practice. Uh practice to to to end this round of rebirth.
